review_notes: I read the whole file. I also checked AddCircle.toCircle in Mathlib/Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Complex/Circle.lean. For T = 0, AddCircle.toCircle_addChar is the constant trivial character, so the module docstring's "for any real T" is slightly loose. The convention is documented on AddCircle.toCircle ("If T = 0 we understand this as the constant function 1"). It is a legitimate junk-value convention, and injectivity is only claimed under T ≠ 0 or via one_ne_zero. The ZMod definitions require [NeZero N], so the domain is not empty and the statements are not vacuous. The roots-of-unity definitions and lemmas (rootsOfUnitytoCircle, rootsOfUnityCircleEquiv, rootsOfUnityAddChar, and the bijectivity and surjectivity results) have consistent hypotheses and express their stated purposes. I found no justified finding under this rubric. I did not look for other kinds of problems.
